Context.description: The situation the persona is in right now.

free_time_minutes.description: How much free time the persona has right now. The single most load-bearing field in the scenario — the same task list can have a different correct answer at 20 minutes vs. 120 minutes.
free_time_minutes.title: Free Time Minutes

current_datetime.description: ISO 8601 timestamp establishing 'now' for this scenario, so task.deadline can be evaluated as near/far/passed.
current_datetime.title: Current Datetime

time_horizon.description: The window the persona is planning within. A CEO scenario will typically use a wider horizon than a Developer scenario.
time_horizon.title: Time Horizon

constraints.description: Any additional situational constraint the model must know about to answer correctly (e.g. 'no meetings can be scheduled'). Empty list when there are none.
constraints.title: Constraints

Context.title: Context

Persona.description: Who the user is, in the terms the system cares about.

role.description: Who the user is (see MIND-01-System-Overview.md role table). Same six values across the whole persona set.
role.title: Role

seniority.description: Only set when seniority genuinely changes the correct answer for this scenario (e.g. a Junior Developer is not expected to pick up an architecture-review task a Senior would). Omit or null otherwise.
seniority.title: Seniority

department.description: Optional, nullable. Some roles (e.g. CEO) are not scoped to a single department; leave null rather than forcing a value.
department.title: Department

Persona.title: Persona

Source.description: Where this scenario came from — for later performance analysis by origin.

type.description: 'real' = hand-written from a genuine (non-Gong) situation; 'AMI'/'FUNSD' = derived from those public corpora; 'synthetic' = fabricated for coverage; 'other' = anything else, explained in source_detail.
type.title: Type

source_detail.description: Free-text pointer to the concrete origin (e.g. an AMI meeting ID). Required in practice when type is 'AMI', 'FUNSD' or 'other'.
source_detail.title: Source Detail

Source.title: Source

Task.description:
A single candidate task within a persona evaluation scenario.

The harness calls `RankingModel.score()` once per Task and builds the ranking
from the returned scores — a model never sees the whole scenario.

task_id.description: Unique within this scenario. Referenced by expected_top_task_id. Same character rule as scenario_id (lowercase, digits, underscore).
task_id.title: Task Id

description.description: Enough detail that a model (and a human reader) can judge duration, urgency and relevance without outside knowledge.
description.title: Description

deadline.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, or null if the task has no hard deadline. Evaluated against context.current_datetime.
deadline.title: Deadline

effort_estimate.description: Effort estimate for the task, in minutes — the eval set's concrete form of the canonical Task.effort_estimate (owned by Inbox). Recorded for Chain's downstream constraint-satisfaction step; the ranking model sees it, but a scenario's correct answer must not hinge on comparing it to context.free_time_minutes (see eval/personas/README.md).
effort_estimate.title: Effort Estimate

tier.description: What KIND of task this is — independent of persona. A Developer can receive an operational or a tactical task; tier is not implied by role. Lowercase values, matching the canonical Task schema (Inbox) and src/mind/scoring/. See 'Persona ≠ Tier' in eval/personas/README.md.
tier.title: Tier

blocked.description: True if this task cannot currently be worked on right now (e.g. waiting on something outside this scenario). A blocked task should generally not be the expected_top_task_id.
blocked.title: Blocked

parent_task_id.description: The task_id of this task's parent in the cross-tier organizational hierarchy (a developer task under a manager task, etc.), matching the canonical Task.parent_task_id. Points outside this scenario, so it is not cross-referenced here. Reserved for the week-7 hierarchical value-propagation evaluation; null in every scenario until then. This is NOT the old same-tier `dependencies` array — that was removed deliberately and is not coming back.
parent_task_id.title: Parent Task Id

Task.title: Task

description:
One fixed evaluation scenario for MIND's persona evaluation harness.

Every scenario in eval/personas/, regardless of persona (Developer, Manager,
Higher Manager, Field Engineer, Salesperson, CEO), conforms to this one
model. Only the values differ between personas — never the structure.

scenario_id.description: Unique identifier across the whole eval/personas/ set. Convention: <role>_<short_slug>, e.g. developer_late_pr_review.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

tasks.description: The candidate tasks the persona is choosing between. At least two, so the scenario actually tests a choice.
tasks.title: Tasks

expected_top_task_id.description: The task_id (from `tasks`) a correct model must pick as the single best use of the persona's free time. Must equal the task_id of exactly one entry in `tasks` (enforced below).
expected_top_task_id.title: Expected Top Task Id

expected_reason.description: Short, checkable explanation of why expected_top_task_id is correct, grounded in per-task signals the ranking model can actually see: a hard deadline, blocked, tier, or an importance/scope judgment from the description. Must NOT hinge on context.free_time_minutes or a duration comparison — that is Chain's concern, not the ranking model's.
expected_reason.title: Expected Reason

team_lead_approved.description: Whether the team lead has reviewed this scenario in a PR and signed off on it. This is the only approval flag on a scenario. Set explicitly by the author: start at false, the team lead (not the author) flips it to true.
team_lead_approved.title: Team Lead Approved
